title: NHLBI tells families to keep a set bedtime, and not to use the bedroom as punishment
summary: NHLBI says children should have a set bedtime and a bedtime routine, and that the child's bedroom should not be used for timeouts or punishment.
body: The habits page says it helps to go to bed and wake up at the same time every day. For children, the wording is a set bedtime and a bedtime routine. The same bullet says not to use the child's bedroom for timeouts or punishment. A later line says to try to keep the schedule on weekends too, and to limit the difference to no more than about an hour, because a late night and a late morning can disrupt the sleep-wake rhythm. This is a habit suggestion from a US institute. It is not a rule that a difficult evening has failed.

sources.title: Sleep Deprivation and Deficiency: Healthy Sleep Habits
